---
title: "Neither Separable nor Inseparable: How Language Models Both Abstract and Entangle Lexeme and Category"
author:
  - name: "Anonymous"
    affiliations:
      - name: "Anonymous Institution"
    email: anon@example.edu
abstract: |
  A word's contextual representation might factor cleanly into a reusable *category* component (e.g.
  \textsc{noun}) and an *item* component (e.g. \emph{dog}), or the two might be entangled. We
  operationalise this as a geometric decomposition of item-by-category representations into marginal
  (item, category) and interaction terms, and measure it across four linguistic distinctions
  spanning grammar and meaning in six pretrained language models. We find that the answer is neither
  "separable" nor "inseparable": the category marginal is cleanly separable from the item marginal
  everywhere, yet a significant, depth-built item-by-category interaction remains that cannot be
  factored back into category plus item. The balance is *graded* across distinctions — strong
  reusable abstraction for part-of-speech, partial for grammatical role, and *absent* for metaphor,
  where the distinction lives only as a per-lexeme interaction. Because the interaction is neither an
  item part nor a category part, developmental "which is learned first" questions and single-direction
  probing are structurally blind to it.

# Methods

## A separability measure {#sec-measure}

For a distinction with items $i \in \{1,\dots,I\}$ (e.g. lemmas) crossed with category levels
$c \in \{1,\dots,C\}$ (e.g. \textsc{noun}/\textsc{verb}), let $M[i,c] \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be the mean
representation of item $i$ used at level $c$. We decompose $M$ additively,

$$
M[i,c] = \mu + \alpha(i) + \beta(c) + \gamma(i,c),
$$ {#eq-decomp}

into a grand mean $\mu$, an **item marginal** $\alpha$ (constant across categories), a **category
marginal** $\beta$ (constant across items), and the **interaction** $\gamma$ — the part of an item's
category-conditioned representation that cannot be predicted from item and category alone. Each term
is obtained by the usual centred projections, giving mutually orthogonal *sources* of variance whose
squared norms partition the between-cell structure.

We report two quantities. **Interaction size** is the interaction's share of the between-cell
structure, $\texttt{size}_\gamma = \lVert\gamma\rVert^2 / (\lVert\alpha\rVert^2 + \lVert\beta\rVert^2 + \lVert\gamma\rVert^2)$.
**Marginal leakage** $\texttt{leak}_{i\to c}$ is the fraction of the item-marginal energy lying in
the category subspace; $\texttt{leak}_{i\to c}\!\approx\!0$ means item and category sit on separate
axes (projecting out the category leaves the item marginal intact).

**Standardisation.** Transformer hidden states contain a few *rogue* dimensions with $10^2$–$10^3\times$
the variance of the rest [@timkey2021bark], which otherwise dominate any raw scatter eigendecomposition.
We $z$-score each dimension before decomposing (a diagonal transform, so it needs no $n\!\gg\!d$
regime, unlike whitening). The measure is therefore invariant to per-dimension rescaling and to
orthogonal rotation, but not to general linear reparametrisation — we do **not** whiten, so that the
identical measure applies to the toy models and the LLMs.

**Denoising and significance.** An interaction magnitude cannot be permutation-tested directly
(shuffling structure does not reduce a sum of squares). We instead estimate $\gamma$ on two
independent halves of the tokens and use the signed cross-product $\langle\gamma_A,\gamma_B\rangle$:
a per-item permutation null gives a significance test, and the cross term denoises the reported size.
We flag an interaction as present only when it is both significant and above a denoised-size floor.

## Constructions and data {#sec-constructions}

We measure four distinctions (@tbl-constructions). Three are **same-token**: the item's surface form
is *identical* across category levels, so the last-subword representation is read from the same token
in every level and there is no tokenisation confound. These carry the argument. The fourth,
morphology, is multi-token (the plural/past is spelled with an extra subword) and enters only as a
control.

| construction | distinction | item | levels | same-token | $n$ |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:-:|--:|
| POS category | noun / verb | lemma | \textsc{noun}/\textsc{verb} | ✓ | 131 |
| POS category | noun / adjective | lemma | \textsc{noun}/\textsc{adj} | ✓ | 27 |
| grammatical role | subject / object | surface form | \textit{nsubj}/\textit{obj} | ✓ | 49 |
| metaphor | literal / metaphorical | surface form | lit/met | ✓ | 180 |
| morphology | number, tense | lemma | Sing/Plur, Pres/Past | ✗ | 200 / 81 |

: The four distinctions. Same-token constructions hold the surface form fixed across category
levels. {#tbl-constructions}

**Identifiability.** The interaction $\gamma(i,c)$ is estimable only for items attested at $\ge 2$
levels; we require $\ge 10$ tokens per cell. For POS this restricts to *convertible* lemmas (words
used as both noun and verb, e.g. \emph{run}, \emph{hit}); role and metaphor have no such restriction
(any noun occurs as subject and object; any content word occurs literally and metaphorically). For
role and metaphor we key the item on the **surface form** rather than the lemma, which guarantees an
identical token across levels (a lemma such as \emph{thing}/\emph{things} can differ in number across
roles, but \emph{things}-subject and \emph{things}-object are the same token).

**Corpora.** POS, role, and morphology use a concatenation of six English Universal Dependencies
treebanks [@nivre2020ud] (EWT, GUM, LinES, ParTUT, GENTLE, PUD; $\approx$706K tokens). Metaphor uses
the VUA20 corpus [@leong2020vua; @steen2010vua], restricted to content words (\textsc{verb},
\textsc{noun}, \textsc{adj}, \textsc{adv}).

**Models.** We use two families at three matched scales each: OPT-BabyLM (trained on child-scale data
[@warstadt2023babylm]) and Pythia (trained on the Pile [@biderman2023pythia]), at 125M/160M,
350M/410M, and 1.3B/1.4B parameters.

**Extraction.** For each token we take the last-subword hidden state at every layer (embeddings
through the final block). Representations are extracted once and the measure is applied offline, per
layer, per construction.

# Results

## Marginals separate, interaction remains {#sec-core}

@tbl-core reports the two quantities at the largest scale of each family (the pattern is
scale-invariant within family). Two things hold simultaneously in every same-token construction.
First, **the marginals separate cleanly**: $\texttt{leak}_{i\to c}\approx 0.001$–$0.018$, so the
reusable category/role direction is nearly orthogonal to the item direction — there is genuine,
portable abstraction. Second, **a significant interaction remains**, and it is *built by
contextualisation*: in every same-token construction the interaction is $\approx 0$ at layer 0
(static embeddings) and grows monotonically with depth. Because the token is identical across levels
*and* absolute position is already encoded at layer 0, the near-zero layer-0 interaction rules out
both the tokenisation and the linear-position confounds; the entanglement is created by the
transformer.

| construction | model | $\texttt{leak}_{i\to c}$ | $\texttt{size}_\gamma$: L0 $\to$ mid $\to$ max |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|
| noun/verb | pythia-1.4b | 0.002 | 0.09 → 0.16 → **0.26** |
| noun/verb | babylm-1.3B | 0.004 | 0.17 → 0.13 → 0.18 |
| noun/adj | pythia-1.4b | 0.011 | 0.06 → 0.10 → **0.16** |
| noun/adj | babylm-1.3B | 0.005 | 0.09 → 0.09 → 0.12 |
| role | pythia-1.4b | 0.003 | **0.001** → 0.045 → 0.10 |
| role | babylm-1.3B | 0.001 | **0.005** → 0.036 → 0.07 |
| metaphor | pythia-1.4b | — | **0.001** → 0.051 → 0.08 |
| metaphor | babylm-1.3B | — | **0.002** → 0.019 → 0.03 |
| morphology | pythia-1.4b | 0.001 | *0.20* → 0.09 → *0.20* |
| morphology | babylm-1.3B | 0.008 | *0.40* → 0.23 → *0.40* |

: Marginal leakage and interaction size (layer 0, middle layer, and maximum over layers). Bold marks
the near-zero layer-0 interaction of the same-token constructions; italics mark the layer-0-peaked
morphology profile (@sec-morph). Metaphor has no defined leakage (no category marginal; @sec-metaphor).
{#tbl-core}

## Abstraction is graded across distinctions {#sec-graded}

Neither "separable" nor "inseparable" describes the representations. They are **both** abstractive
and entangling, and the balance depends on the distinction. Part-of-speech has a strong reusable
category marginal *and* a large depth-growing interaction. Grammatical role has a smaller but real
reusable marginal and a smaller interaction. **Metaphor has no reusable marginal at all**: the
category main effect $\beta$ is $\approx 0$ and not significant, so $\texttt{leak}_{i\to c}$ is
undefined — there is no shared "metaphor direction." The metaphor signal is entirely the per-lexeme
interaction $\gamma$.

## Metaphor: no shared axis, only a per-word interaction {#sec-metaphor}

We confirm the metaphor result with linear probes at the top layer (pythia-410m; @tbl-probe). A
**pooled** literal/metaphorical probe reaches 0.79 accuracy, but this is *word identity*: words differ
in metaphor base-rate, so decoding which word predicts metaphoricity for free. Removing word identity
by **centring each word** collapses the probe to chance (0.53) — there is no shared metaphor axis,
consistent with $\beta\approx 0$. A **per-word** probe, however, recovers 0.69 (76% of words above
0.6, growing with depth; e.g. *course* 0.96, *account* 0.95, *plant* 0.92): metaphoricity *is* encoded,
but word-specifically, pointing in a different direction for each lexeme. This is exactly the
significant, depth-growing $\gamma$, and it argues against metaphor being "literal + a uniform
coercion operator" in the sense of a compositional generative lexicon [@pustejovsky1995generative],
which would appear as a shared $\beta$.

| probe | accuracy | interpretation |
|:--|--:|:--|
| pooled lit/met | 0.79 | word identity / base-rate |
| globally word-centred | 0.53 | no shared metaphor axis ($\approx$ chance) |
| per-word | 0.69 | word-specific signal (the interaction) |

: Metaphor probes at the top layer (pythia-410m); chance = 0.50. {#tbl-probe}

## Morphology: a tokenisation confound {#sec-morph}

Regular number/tense show the same marginal separability ($\texttt{leak}_{i\to c}\approx
0.001$–$0.008$) and a real interaction, but the depth profile **inverts**: the interaction *peaks at
layer 0* and dips with depth (@tbl-core, italics). This is the tokenisation confound — the plural/past
is read at a *different subword* (dog vs dog-\textbf{s}), so the layer-0 interaction reflects token
identity, not morphology. It is the mirror image of the same-token profile, which is why the
same-token constructions carry the argument. A genuinely zero-marked control (\emph{cut}/\emph{hit},
\emph{sheep}/\emph{fish}) is positive but underpowered ($n=3$–4 lemmas).

## Family difference {#sec-family}

Across POS, role, and metaphor, Pythia builds more interaction with depth than BabyLM/OPT, whose
profile is flatter and, for the multi-token POS grid, layer-0-heavy. Part of BabyLM's layer-0 mass is
plausibly an OPT *absolute*-positional-embedding artifact (vs Pythia's rotary embeddings), which
appears at the embedding layer; we state the family difference as a hypothesis, not an established
effect, as it is confounded by architecture and training-data scale together.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The measurement reframes an old dichotomy [@houghton2024exemplars; @tomasello2003constructing].
Rather than asking whether a model *abstracts* categories or *stores exemplars*, we quantify how much
of a distinction is a reusable component (the marginals) versus an item-bound conjunction (the
interaction, superposed onto the shared code [@elhage2022superposition]), and find real models sit in
between — with a balance that shifts across linguistic dimensions. Two standard methods are
structurally blind to the entangled part. Developmental "which is learned first" questions presuppose
that the representation partitions into an item part and a category part; the interaction is neither,
so for it the ordering question has no referent. Single-direction probing [@hewitt2019structural]
recovers the category marginal but not the interaction — and for metaphor, where the marginal does not
exist, would wrongly conclude the distinction is not represented. The interaction is precisely where
the exemplar-versus-abstraction tension lives, and it is exactly what those methods cannot see.
